_doc: P3 LO map for the 225 live V2 questions (45 stem templates x 5 variants). concept = subtopic; one LO per stem template. review: null = structurally unambiguous; otherwise flagged for clinician (Mike) review. Titles are draft wording, not clinician-approved.

Peripheral nerve anatomy: Identify the median (recurrent motor) branch lesion causing loss of thumb opposition
Lower-limb anatomy: Identify the sciatic/common peroneal injury causing foot drop after posterior hip dislocation
Neck anatomy: Identify recurrent laryngeal nerve injury as the cause of post-thyroidectomy hoarseness
Upper-limb anatomy: Identify the nerve/muscle responsible for initiating arm abduction (first 15 degrees)
Template wording mixes 'nerve' and muscle initiation (supraspinatus/suprascapular); confirm intended LO
Neuroanatomy: Localise a hemicord (Brown-Sequard) lesion from dissociated sensory loss
Cardiovascular physiology: Explain the immediate baroreflex response to acute haemorrhage
Respiratory physiology: Explain factors that right-shift the oxyhaemoglobin curve during exercise
Renal physiology: Explain ADH-dependent urine concentration in dehydration
Acid-base physiology: Describe the respiratory compensation to metabolic acidosis
Endocrine physiology: Explain insulin-mediated postprandial glucose uptake and storage
Hepatic biochemistry: Recognise defective bilirubin conjugation (e.g. Gilbert) in unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia
Metabolic biochemistry: Identify fatty-acid oxidation defects as a cause of hypoketotic fasting hypoglycaemia
Mitochondrial metabolism: Explain lactic acidosis from impaired mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
Overlaps Vitamin biochemistry (thiamine -> lactic acidosis) and Mitochondrial genetics; confirm whether these are one LO or prerequisite-linked
Energy metabolism: Recognise a muscle energy-metabolism defect (e.g. McArdle) from exertional cramps and raised CK
Vitamin biochemistry: Identify thiamine deficiency (PDH cofactor) in alcohol use with neurological signs and lactic acidosis
Overlaps Mitochondrial metabolism; possible prerequisite relationship
Autonomic pharmacology: Attribute beta-blocker bradycardia to beta-1 receptor blockade
Renin-angiotensin pharmacology: Explain ACE-inhibitor cough via bradykinin accumulation
Opioid pharmacology: Attribute opioid toxidrome to mu-receptor agonism
Anticoagulant pharmacology: Use INR to monitor/reverse warfarin effect
Renal pharmacology: Recognise drug-induced hyperkalaemia from impaired aldosterone-mediated K+ excretion
Drug class unspecified in template (ACEi/ARB/spironolactone/amiloride); confirm LO scope
Pulmonary pathology: Identify emphysema as alveolar wall destruction in smokers
Neoplastic pathology: State that invasion (not size/growth) establishes malignancy
Cellular adaptation: Identify hypertrophy as the adaptation to pressure overload
Cell injury: Explain ischaemic (ATP-depletion) tubular cell injury after hypotension
Possible prerequisite link to Renal physiology; confirm
Urinary microbiology: Identify E. coli as the commonest uropathogen
Respiratory microbiology: Identify Streptococcus pneumoniae from lobar pneumonia and lancet diplococci
Gastrointestinal microbiology: Identify Clostridioides difficile after broad-spectrum antibiotics
CNS microbiology: Identify Neisseria meningitidis from meningism with purpura
Template states the diagnosis in the stem (answer cue); item-quality review
Fungal host defence: Explain T-cell (cell-mediated) defence against mucosal Candida
Overlaps Immunology > Cell-mediated immunity; confirm concept placement
Humoral immunity: Link absent B cells to impaired antibody production (e.g. XLA)
Transplant immunology: Recognise hyperacute rejection from preformed antibodies
Cell-mediated immunity: Recognise type IV (delayed, T-cell) hypersensitivity in contact dermatitis
Chromosomal genetics: Identify trisomy 21 as a numerical chromosomal abnormality
Inheritance: Recognise X-linked recessive inheritance from a pedigree
Molecular genetics: Classify a single-base substitution changing one amino acid as missense
Developmental genetics: Infer germline (pre-zygotic) origin from a constitutional variant
Neurulation: Link neural tube defects to failed neural tube closure
Cardiac embryology: Link septal defects to abnormal partitioning of the primitive heart
Template does not specify the defect; LO is broad - confirm granularity
Gastrointestinal embryology: Link intestinal atresia to failed recanalisation
Renal embryology: Identify the ureteric bud as essential for metanephric kidney development
Head and neck embryology: Identify the pharyngeal arch (hillocks of His) origin of the auricle
